title: Protects against unintended coercion of references to container types to &dyn Any when the container type dereferences to a dyn Any which could be directly referenced instead.
summary: The intention is usually to get a reference to the dyn Any the value dereferences to, rather than coercing a reference to the container itself to &dyn Any. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: We used to think it measured how hard a method is to understand.
summary: Ideally, we would like to be able to measure how hard a function is to understand given its context (what we call its Cognitive Complexity). But that’s not what this lint does. See “Known problems” Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for collapsible else { if ... } expressions that can be collapsed to else if ....
summary: Each if-statement adds one level of nesting, which makes code look more complex than it really is. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for nested if statements which can be collapsed by &&-combining their conditions.
summary: Each if-statement adds one level of nesting, which makes code look more complex than it really is. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Finds nested match or if let expressions where the patterns may be “collapsed” together without adding any branches.
summary: It is unnecessarily verbose and complex. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for consecutive calls to str::replace (2 or more) that can be collapsed into a single call.
summary: Consecutive str::replace calls scan the string multiple times with repetitive code. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for collections that are never queried.
summary: Putting effort into constructing a collection but then never querying it might indicate that the author forgot to do whatever they intended to do with the collection. Example: Clone a vector, sort it for iteration, but then mistakenly iterate the original vector instead. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks comparison chains written with if that can be rewritten with match and cmp.
summary: if is not guaranteed to be exhaustive and conditionals can get repetitive Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for comparing to an empty slice such as "" or [], and suggests using .is_empty() where applicable.
summary: Some structures can answer .is_empty() much faster than checking for equality. So it is good to get into the habit of using .is_empty(), and having it is cheap. Besides, it makes the intent clearer than a manual comparison in some contexts. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for casts of a primitive method pointer like max/min to any integer type.
summary: Casting a function pointer to an integer can have surprising results and can occur accidentally if parentheses are omitted from a function call. If you aren’t doing anything low-level with function pointers then you can opt out of casting functions to integers in order to avoid mistakes. Alternatively, you can use this lint to audit all uses of function pointer casts in your code. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: It identifies calls to .is_empty() on constant values.
summary: String literals and constant values are known at compile time. Checking if they are empty will always return the same value. This might not be the intention of the expression. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for types that implement Copy as well as Iterator.
summary: Implicit copies can be confusing when working with iterator combinators. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.
